body.statement: Under \(\texttt{thm:generic-bic-component-recovery}\), fix finite \(\mathcal Q\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Then \(\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n)\) converges in probability to \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) in Hausdorff distance. Retaining state labels before removing coincident numerical values, the confidence collection satisfies \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\left\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\text{ and every }g_E(\Sigma_0),\ E\in\mathcal R(C),\text{ belongs to its labelled interval in }\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\right\}\geq1-\alpha.\] The conclusion permits duplicate effect values and singular joint effect covariance.
body.justification: The observationally recovered object is a finite set of member-labelled causal effects, so inference must cover every component member.
body.gap: NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 derives joint effect inference across ordinary equivalence classes, and StriederDrton2023 uses test inversion under equal variances; neither treats equality-constrained coefficient blocks after exact blocked-component selection.
body.consumer: A causal-community analysis can report simultaneous uncertainty for all total effects compatible with its recovered singleton-permitting component.
